name: Computer Running Slowly
description: Diagnose common causes of poor Windows performance using safe, evidence-based checks.

confirm_windows.title: Confirm the Windows device
confirm_windows.instruction: Save open work before beginning. This workflow uses Windows tools and does not require installing additional software.
confirm_windows.help_text: Preserving work first makes later restart and update steps safer.

unsupported_platform.title: Use a workflow for this operating system
unsupported_platform.message: This performance workflow is designed for Windows. Choose a platform-specific workflow or update the active device profile before continuing.

identify_scope.question: What feels slow?
identify_scope.help_text: A single slow application usually has a different cause than system-wide poor performance.

restart_application.title: Restart the affected application
restart_application.instruction: Save work in the application, close it completely, wait ten seconds, and open it again. Do not end unfamiliar background processes.

application_improved.question: Is the application responding normally now?

resolved_application.title: Application performance restored
resolved_application.message: Restarting the application cleared its temporary state. Save work regularly and note whether the slowdown returns after a specific action.

application_specific.title: Application-specific investigation needed
application_specific.message: The rest of Windows may be healthy. Check the application's updates, add-ons, file size, network dependency, and support documentation before changing system-wide settings.

check_recent_restart.question: Has the computer been restarted since the slowdown began?
check_recent_restart.help_text: Restart is different from closing the laptop lid or signing out.

restart_windows.title: Restart Windows safely
restart_windows.instruction: Save all work, open Start, select Power, and choose Restart. Sign back in and allow two minutes for startup activity to settle.
restart_windows.help_text: A controlled restart reloads Windows services and clears temporary resource problems.

restart_improved.question: Is the computer performing normally after the restart?

resolved_restart.title: Temporary performance issue cleared
resolved_restart.message: The restart restored normal performance. If the issue returns, note which application or activity was running immediately beforehand.

inspect_task_manager.title: Inspect resource use in Task Manager
inspect_task_manager.instruction: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc. On the Processes page, wait about 30 seconds, then compare the CPU, Memory, and Disk columns. Do not end unfamiliar Windows processes.
inspect_task_manager.help_text: Task Manager shows which resource is under sustained pressure and which process is using it.

identify_bottleneck.question: Which Task Manager resource remains unusually high?
identify_bottleneck.help_text: Look for sustained use rather than a brief spike while an application opens.

reduce_active_workload.title: Reduce the active workload
reduce_active_workload.instruction: Save your work and close applications you recognize but are not currently using. In Task Manager, leave Windows processes and unfamiliar items alone.
reduce_active_workload.help_text: Closing known applications is reversible and tests whether the slowdown is caused by the current workload.

workload_improved.question: Did performance improve after closing unused applications?

resolved_workload.title: Active workload identified
resolved_workload.message: Running applications were placing the system under resource pressure. Reopen only what is needed and monitor Task Manager to identify the application that causes sustained high use.

check_storage.title: Check available storage
check_storage.instruction: Open Settings, select System, then Storage. Note the free space on the Windows drive without deleting anything yet.

storage_result.question: Is the Windows drive nearly full?
storage_result.help_text: Less than about 10 percent free space is a useful warning sign, especially when Windows is updating or using virtual memory.

safe_storage_cleanup.title: Free space with Windows recommendations
safe_storage_cleanup.instruction: In Settings > System > Storage, open Cleanup recommendations. Review each category and remove only files you recognize and no longer need. Do not manually delete Windows or Program Files folders.
safe_storage_cleanup.help_text: Windows cleanup recommendations are safer than deleting system folders manually.

cleanup_improved.question: After cleanup and a restart, has performance improved?

resolved_storage.title: Low storage was affecting performance
resolved_storage.message: Freeing storage restored working space for Windows, updates, and temporary files. Keep important personal files backed up and review storage periodically.

review_startup_apps.title: Review startup applications
review_startup_apps.instruction: Open Task Manager, select Startup apps, and sort by Startup impact. Disable only optional applications you recognize and do not need immediately after sign-in. Leave security, accessibility, driver, and workplace management tools enabled.
review_startup_apps.help_text: Startup apps compete for resources at the same time and can make sign-in feel slow.

startup_changes.question: Did you find optional high-impact startup applications to disable?

restart_after_startup.title: Test the lighter startup
restart_after_startup.instruction: Restart Windows, sign in, and wait two minutes. Then test the tasks that previously felt slow.

startup_improved.question: Did reducing startup load improve performance?

resolved_startup.title: Startup load reduced
resolved_startup.message: Optional startup applications were consuming resources after sign-in. They remain installed and can still be opened when needed.

run_security_scan.title: Run a Windows Security quick scan
run_security_scan.instruction: Open Windows Security, select Virus & threat protection, and run a Quick scan. Keep the device connected to power and follow only the actions recommended by Windows Security.
run_security_scan.help_text: A built-in malware scan checks for unwanted software without requiring an unfamiliar download.

security_followup.title: Security follow-up required
security_followup.message: Follow the remediation shown by Windows Security or contact your support team. Avoid entering sensitive information until detected threats are handled and the device is rescanned.

check_updates.title: Check Windows Update
check_updates.instruction: Open Settings > Windows Update and select Check for updates. Review available updates, but save work before installing or restarting.
check_updates.help_text: Updates can resolve known performance, reliability, and driver problems.

install_updates.title: Install approved updates
install_updates.instruction: Save work, connect the computer to power, install the available Windows updates, and restart when prompted. On a managed workplace device, follow your organization's update policy.

updates_improved.question: Is performance acceptable after updates and restart?

resolved_updates.title: Updates restored performance
resolved_updates.message: A Windows or driver update corrected the performance problem. Continue normal update maintenance and monitor for recurrence.

escalate_performance.title: Deeper performance diagnostics recommended
escalate_performance.message: The safe first-line checks did not isolate the cause. Record the slow task, Task Manager resource levels, available storage, scan result, and update status for a technician. Hardware health, event logs, drivers, or application profiling may require deeper review.
